data.narrative:
INTALUS, a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company, has raised $31M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 peers across robotics and manufacturing—1 public (277810.KQ) and 8 private firms including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics—though direct peer-median benchmarking was constrained by insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow subset.

The Stage-Progression method, the primary applicable approach, applies a standard 2.5x step-up multiplier to the $31M raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $78M. This reflects typical capital accumulation and value creation from Seed to subsequent rounds in the sector. Peer-median triangulation was not deployed due to insufficient datapoints (fewer than 3 comps) in tightly filtered buckets; the broader 10-company sector universe lacks sufficient granularity at INTALUS's specific stage and tier.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $66M to $89M, with a median of $78M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression point estimate. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrowly comparable Seed-stage peers in robotics and manufacturing, which limits confidence in peer-derived multiples, and the reliance on raised capital as a valuation proxy rather than revenue or profitability metrics. Additional revenue traction or customer validation would refine the upper bound; conversely, extended fundraising timelines or market softness could pressure the range downward.
